title: Iterative program-planning homework with transformer-driven test feedback
summary: CS1 students write to-do-list plans for nine functions across theater seating, music playlists, and restaurant ordering. For two functions, a GPT-4 pipeline translates each plan into Python and returns test results so students can revise up to five times.

sources.title: Iterative Student Program Planning using Transformer-Driven Feedback
sources.evidence_quote: We developed three problem scenarios, each with three functions for which students had to write plans.

context.learner_level: novice programmers in week three of CS1

assessment.summary: Write natural-language plans for nine programming functions before learning enough syntax to implement them.
student_actions: Decompose each function into an ordered to-do-list plan.
Submit plans for theater, playlist, and restaurant scenarios.
Use test-case feedback on two designated functions to revise a plan up to five times.

outputs.artifact: Likert response before each revised feedback-plan submission

student_role.description: Students receive test outcomes from code that GPT-4 generates from their plans; they do not see the generated code or direct LLM commentary.

allowed_purposes: Translate plans into hidden executable code for test feedback
prohibited_actions: Direct LLM feedback or repair suggestions on the plan

assessment_system_role: Translate a student plan step by step into Python without correcting plan errors
Run staff tests and return pass/fail feedback
